explanation: States that every Hausdorff topological 3-manifold (ChartedSpace over ℝ³) homotopy equivalent to S³ is homeomorphic to S³. Compactness is not assumed, but it is implied: a non-compact connected n-manifold has H_n(M; ℤ/2) = 0 (this needs only Hausdorff and locally Euclidean), so it cannot be homotopy equivalent to Sⁿ. Second countability then follows from compactness. Requiring Hausdorffness rules out non-Hausdorff counterexamples. The statement is the Millennium problem solved by Perelman and is correctly tagged solved.
